paper_title: Long-baseline quantum sensor network as dark matter haloscope
suggested_experiment_name: AMAILS (Atomic Magnetometer Arrays in Large Shields)
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing epsilon, dimensionless, as plotted on y-axis
notes: AMAILS: network of 15 SERF atomic magnetometers in two 2m shielded rooms (Suzhou/Harbin, 1692 km baseline) searching for dark photon dark matter over 1-500 Hz (4.1 feV - 2.1 peV). Only one explicit numerical limit is given in the text: epsilon ~ 5e-6 at 2.1 peV (500 Hz). The low-mass endpoint value (2.5e-3 at 4.1 feV) is estimated by scaling epsilon ~ 1/m_A' from Eq. (1) (B-field signal proportional to epsilon*m_A' with roughly flat magnetometer noise floor), consistent with the exclusion curve slope in Fig. 3b; it is an approximation, not a paper-stated value. Full exclusion curve is only in Fig. 3b (no table). Paper also shows a future projection (~6 orders of magnitude better) which is NOT included in data_points. DM density assumed rho = 0.45 GeV/cm^3. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 37)) | Vision: Fig. 3b of arXiv:2305.00890 (Jiang et al.). Blue-shaded region is excluded at 95% C.L. from the 15-magnetometer Suzhou-Harbin network over dark-photon mass 4.1 feV to 2.1 peV (Compton frequency 1-500 Hz). Anchors: text quotes epsilon ~ 5e-6 at 2.1 peV; left edge of exclusion rises to ~1e-2 at 4.1 feV. Narrow spikes near 50 Hz harmonics (~2.1e-13 eV and multiples) degrade the limit locally (one bump at 2.0e-13 eV included; taller narrow spikes up to ~1e-2 at ~4.6e-13 eV not fully traced). Overlapping regions (SNIPE, Earth, Jupiter, Cavendish-Coulomb) and dashed astrophysical lines (CMB, plasma heating) excluded from trace.
